sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: accidents and emergency situations
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
Crash-scene duties on the first chapter page use must for stopping, moving, staying and exchanging information and should for notifying police; C keeps each verb as printed [A01].
The roadside emergency tips on the roadside page are described as guidelines not necessarily required by law, so the triangle distances there are taught as advice and are not merged with the warning-device rules in the safe-operation chapter [A03] (verify IN-CRASH-D-TRIANGLE).
Traffic stop items are suggestions in the manual, except the license, registration and insurance requirement and the officer documentation duty, which it states as requirements.

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 65 advises placing a reflective triangle two hundred feet behind the vehicle, or five hundred on a hill or curve, while physical page 62 gives one-hundred-foot placements for disabled vehicles; the manual frames page 65 as guidance, so both are taught on their own page until the BMV confirms how the exam treats them.
